text:
maria: opening thread for a small follow-up on capability manifests and emergency fallback semantics. want a compact, machine-readable manifest that adapters and SDKs can evaluate fast. goal: avoid ambiguous behavior in the field.
kevin: agree. high level: manifest should enumerate required vs optional features with fallback_policy. required -> reject request if unavailable. optional -> either degrade silently or return a warning based on policy.
tariq: proposal for shape (pseudocode):
```
capability_manifest {
  version: 1,
  features: [
    { name: "streaming", tier: "optional", fallback_policy: "shim_queue" },
    { name: "kvcache", tier: "optional", fallback_policy: "cold_path" },
    { name: "kms_local", tier: "required", fallback_policy: "deny" }
  ],
  entitlements: { gpu_burst: "plan:pro", private_kms: "plan:enterprise" }
}
```
maria: +1. Important: fallback_policy needs a small taxonomy we can index: shim_queue, cold_path, host_proxy, deny. keep it intentionally small so ops can reason about cost/latency.
kevin: add `degradation_hint` (human friendly) and `metric_tags` so adapters auto-add tags when fallback is used. e.g., `metric_tags: ["fallback=shim", "feature=streaming"]`.
tariq: backward compat: adapters must accept older manifests and map unknown fallback_policy to `deny` by default (safe). SDKs should treat a missing manifest as `floor-only` with metric `manifest_absent`.
maria: security entitlement validation: manifest's entitlements are authoritative but adapters must validate token scopes before granting ceilings. if token lacks scope, return HTTP 403 with body { code: "ENTITLEMENT_MISSING", upgrade_url: "https://console/..." }. ops: prefer quick failure over silent fallback for privilege errors.
ops-bot: deployment note: rolling-canary started for manifest-v1 -> hosted/eu-central (20%) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
kevin: test matrix notes: simulate KMS outage, measure error vs latency for each fallback_policy. shim_queue might increase tail latency; cold_path hurts throughput. we should set alert thresholds accordingly.
devx: SDK ergonomics: expose `capabilities` object on client instance. e.g., `client.capabilities.has('streaming')` and event `on('capability_change', ...)`. Also surface `capability_origin` (manifest vs runtime_probe).
tariq: runtime_probe idea: besides manifest handshake, adapters can run quick probes for certain features (e.g., small streaming probe) and report `runtime_status` in handshake response: `ok`, `degraded`, `down`. SDKs should cache that for N seconds.
maria: ops/runbook: add three actionable codes for app owners: FALLBACK_OK (no action), FALLBACK_DEGRADE (monitor for perf regressions), FALLBACK_BLOCK (contact infra). map these to incident severity. i'll draft runbook and sample alerts.
kevin: one more: define an explicit error header `X-Redwood-Feature-Result: streaming=denied;reason=entitlement` so non-JSON clients can still react.
devx: will prototype SDK surface and emit a short compatibility guide for app teams (how to handle disabled ceilings). target PR next week.
maria: thanks team. i'll compile manifest proto + enum list + runbook into a short RFC. we should aim for a conservative rollout: manifest-v1 enabled for new adapters first, then a canary for sidecars in dedicated, then wide rollout. closing notes: prefer explicit reject for security-sensitive features, allow graceful degrade for cache/routing optimizations.
